Read feedback tips +
  • If an instruction is unclear, encourage her to ask for a demonstration or an example of when to use it.
  • Let her try the suggestion in practice or a match, then tell her coach what felt different.
  • Ask what she understood and wants to try. Every journey home doesn’t need to become an analysis of mistakes.
02 / FOOTBALL & EVERYDAY LIFE

A week that works for her.

School, friendships, rest and football all need room in her week.

Read balance tips +
  • Plan football around school commitments and time to relax.
  • Choose home practice that fits her week. Extra work should have a useful focus.
  • Tell STAR when she feels overloaded or needs a lighter session so we can discuss the plan together.
03 / CONFIDENCE & ENJOYMENT

Let her set the direction.

Her goals can be ambitious, small or changing. Start by asking what matters to her.

Read confidence tips +
  • Ask: “What would make football feel good for you this season?” Agree a next step with her.
  • Notice when pressure is taking away the enjoyment. Listen before offering solutions.
  • If she wants a change or a break, explore what she means and respect her choice. Goals can change.

What ages does STAR coach?
description: STAR offers girls’ football coaching for ages 5–18. Sparks groups are for ages 5–10 and Development Groups for ages 11–16. Individual options include Flyers for ages 7–10, and Prestige or flexible one-to-one coaching for ages 11–18.

title: Is STAR suitable for complete beginners?
description: Yes. We coach girls of all abilities, including complete beginners. We shape the coaching around your daughter’s experience and what helps her learn.

title: How does STAR support neurodivergent players?
description: STAR is an Approved Autism Friendly Coaching provider. We discuss your daughter’s needs with you and agree what helps her learn and feel comfortable. Read about individual support.

title: Where does STAR football coaching take place?
description: STAR provides girls’ football coaching in Taunton and Wellington, Somerset. The venue depends on the programme and individual arrangements. We’ll confirm the location and availability with you before her first session.

title: What should she bring to a STAR football session?
description: Bring a drink and comfortable sports clothing. We’ll confirm the venue, playing surface, suitable footwear and any session-specific kit requirements before her first coaching session.

title: What if my daughter feels nervous about coaching?
description: Tell us what worries her and what helps her settle. We can explain what will happen before she arrives and discuss an introduction that helps her feel comfortable asking questions and trying new skills.

title: Can I stay and watch?
description: Ask STAR about arrangements for her session. We’ll confirm where to meet, whether you can stay and the best place to watch at the agreed venue.

title: Does STAR replace her football club?
description: No. STAR is an independent development centre offering additional coaching alongside her existing club. The aim is to help her apply what she learns in team training and matches.

title: How is her football development reviewed?
description: We set clear coaching priorities, give practical feedback and listen to her experience. Structured individual programmes include an Individual Development Plan (IDP) and regular reviews. Each programme page explains the support included.
